failure_summary.description: First searches emitted as bare calls with no assignment/save, as a nested search inside save_to_cache, as a duplicated search, with an invented kwarg (query_summary), or with import/if-None blocks (trajectories 1, 4, 6, 7, 8).
A US state abbreviation (OR, GA) was put in city= instead of state=.

Cache already had the domain (flights/return_flights, restaurants, attractions), yet the model re-ran a search instead of load -> filter -> save (class answer, formal/Italian answer, named-place question).
Round-trip flight dates produced one search or one one-leg search instead of two separate outbound/return searches, and the airport-code habit (SJC) was not mapped to start_airport/end_airport.
'solo trip' was turned into num_people=1, which the user never stated as a number.

patch.reasoning: The skill already has rules for most of these cases, but they are scattered across a very long document and the model keeps ignoring them. The edits add short, example-driven rules placed where the failures happen. First, a compact set of copy-exactly templates at the top fixes the structural errors (bare calls, nested calls, imports, if/else, invented kwargs, state in city, num_people from 'solo'). Second, a round-trip example covers two-leg flight searches plus airport-code mapping. Third, worked examples for 'cache exists, so filter' cover a flight-class answer, a style/cuisine answer, and a named-place question.

edits.target: (No learned rules yet. Rules will be added through the reflection process.)
edits.content:
## Output templates (copy these shapes exactly; most failures come from breaking them)
- FIRST SEARCH = exactly two lines, never bare, never nested:
  `attractions = search_attractions(state="OR", type=["Social"])`
  `save_to_cache(key="attractions", value=attractions)`
  WRONG: `search_attractions(...)` with no assignment; `save_to_cache(key="x", value=search_x(...))`; calling the same search twice.
- REFINEMENT = exactly three lines: `x = get_results_from_cache(key="<key literally in CACHE>")`, `y = filter_<domain>(prior_results=x, <only the new constraint>)`, `save_to_cache(key="filtered_<domain>", value=y)`.
- The code block holds ONLY tool calls. No `import` / `from ... import` (e.g. `from cache import ...` fails), no `if ... is None`, no else, no loops, no print, no explanatory comments.
- Use only kwargs listed for that tool in TOOL CONFIG. `query_summary` is an OUTPUT field, never an input; passing it raises a ValidationError. Never pass descriptions or free text.
- A US state name or 2-letter abbreviation ('OR', 'GA', 'Georgia') ALWAYS goes in `state=`, never `city=`. 'trip to GA, Guided and Historical attractions' -> `search_attractions(state="GA", type=["Guided", "Historical"])`.
- Party words without a number ('solo trip', 'couple', 'family') are NOT num_people. Pass num_people / num_rooms only when the user states a number. Hotel with 'solo trip', budget 40, Nov 8-14 -> `search_hotels(city="Raleigh", budget=40, checkin_date=["November 8, 2025"], checkout_date=["November 14, 2025"])`, nothing else.

edits.target: ## Rule 9: Round-trip flights (+ hotel) are separate search calls
edits.content:
- Worked example (flights only, no hotel): 'weekend getaway to Memphis from Lexington' then 'depart May 14, 2025 and return May 16, 2025' -> TWO assigned and saved searches, never one:
  `flights = search_flights(start_airport_city="Lexington", end_airport_city="Memphis", departure_date=["May 14, 2025"])`
  `save_to_cache(key="flights", value=flights)`
  `return_flights = search_flights(start_airport_city="Memphis", end_airport_city="Lexington", departure_date=["May 16, 2025"])`
  `save_to_cache(key="return_flights", value=return_flights)`
  A date pair in the last turn always means an outbound search and a return search with the cities swapped, even when the conversation only mentions flights or a 'getaway'.
- Airport habit ('I normally fly from SJC') adds only `start_airport="SJC"` on the outbound search and `end_airport="SJC"` on the return search. The cities stay as city names. Do not add cache probes, imports or if-blocks.

edits.target: ## Rule 13: Refinement precision and code hygiene (supplements Rule 2)
edits.content:
- If the CACHE holds ANY flight key ('flights', 'return_flights', 'departure_flights', filtered ones), the reply to a class/airline/time question is NEVER search_flights. Example: CACHE has 'flights' and 'return_flights'; last turn 'We prefer business class' ->
  `f = get_results_from_cache(key="flights")`
  `ff = filter_flights(prior_results=f, flight_class=["business"])`
  `save_to_cache(key="filtered_flights", value=ff)`
  `r = get_results_from_cache(key="return_flights")`
  `rf = filter_flights(prior_results=r, flight_class=["business"])`
  `save_to_cache(key="filtered_return_flights", value=rf)`
  Both legs are filtered. Do not pass cities or dates to the filter.

edits.target: ## Rule 10: Route the LAST turn's constraints to the right domain; a 'yes' to a proposal is a new constraint
edits.content:
- If a domain already has a CACHE key, an answer about its style, cuisine, rating or place is ALWAYS load -> filter -> save, never a new search. Example: CACHE 'restaurants' (Memphis) and last turn 'Something formal, with a good Italian menu' -> `r = get_results_from_cache(key="restaurants")`, `r2 = filter_restaurants(prior_results=r, cuisine=["Italian"])`, `save_to_cache(key="filtered_restaurants", value=r2)`. 'Formal' produces no param.
- If the assistant's last message proposed a specific named place (e.g. 'Have you considered Ashland Park?') and the user asks about it ('No, I haven't. What's there?'), treat the name as a neighborhood constraint on the cached attractions: `a = get_results_from_cache(key="attractions")`, `a2 = filter_attractions(prior_results=a, neighborhood=["Ashland Park"])`, `save_to_cache(key="neighborhood_attractions", value=a2)`. Do not re-run search_attractions and do not repeat the city or type already shown in the CACHE summary.
